questions.question: What is a function of a random variable determined by $g$?
What does a function of a random variable do?
options: It removes all randomness from the model
It makes the sample space empty
It changes every probability into a count.
It transforms the random outcome into a new quantity.

questions.question: If $X$ is a random variable and $g$ is measurable, what can be said about $g(X)$?
options: It is never a random variable
It is again a random variable

questions.question: Can the distribution of $g(X)$ differ from the distribution of $X$?
options: Only if $g$ is the identity function

questions.question: What tool can compute expectations of $g(X)$ without deriving the full distribution of $g(X)$?
If $X$ is temperature in Celsius, what does a linear function of $X$ give?
options: The probability of a birthday match
The support of a Bernoulli variable

questions.question: If $X$ is a return, what does $X^2$ measure?
options: The original return sign only, ignoring magnitude

questions.question: If $X$ is a waiting time, which is a function of $X$?
options: The set of all customers with no condition
An indicator of whether $X$ exceeds ten minutes
The sample space before $X$ is defined

questions.question: If $X=3$ and $g(x)=x^2$, what is $g(X)$?
If $Y=2X+1$ and $X=4$, what is $Y$?
Why is $g(X)$ useful when the observed value is derived from another random value?
options: It makes the original variable deterministic.
It lets the derived quantity be a random variable.
It prevents any distribution from changing

questions.question: Why might $g(X)$ have a different distribution from $X$?
options: The function can merge, stretch, or transform values of $X$
The sample space must change to the empty set
The function must always be one-to-one

questions.question: What is the role of measurability in the statement about $g(X)$?
options: It ensures $g(X)$ is a valid random variable.

questions.question: If $X$ is a die roll and $Y=X^2$, what values can $Y$ take?
If $X$ is waiting time and $Y=\mathbf 1_{\{X>10\}}$, what are the possible values of $Y$?
If $X$ is Celsius temperature and $Y=\frac95X+32$, what kind of transformation is this?
options: A linear function of a random variable
A partition of the sample space

questions.question: Why does $Y=g(X)$ remain random even though $g$ is deterministic?
options: A deterministic function cannot be applied to random variables
The output must equal the sample space
The distribution of $Y$ is always degenerate
The input $X$ is random, so the output changes with the random outcome

questions.question: Computing $E[g(X)]$ directly from $X$'s distribution avoids a costly intermediate step. Which step does LOTUS avoid?
options: It requires first finding a closed-form density for $g(X)$.
It applies only when $g$ is a one-to-one transformation.
It replaces expectation by the most likely value of $g(X)$.
It computes $E[g(X)]$ from the distribution of $X$ directly.

questions.question: If $X$ takes values $-1$ and $1$, and $Y=X^2$, what is true about $Y$?
If $X$ is a return and $Y=X^2$, what information does $Y$ lose compared with $X$?
